images.alt: A Hewlett-Packard HP 9000 B180L workstation with its 20-inch HP A4033A colour CRT monitor, keyboard and mouse, running HP-UX 10.20
images.caption: An HP 9000 Visualize B180L — the same B-class desktop chassis as the B160L emulated here, one speed grade up — with HP's 20-inch monitor, running HP-UX 10.20.

images.alt: A Hewlett-Packard HP 9000 B180L workstation set-up with its HP A4033A 20-inch CRT, PS/2 keyboard and mouse, running HP-UX 10.20
images.caption: The complete B-class desk: system unit, HP monitor, PS/2 keyboard and mouse — the hardware the Visualize line was sold as in 1996–97.

images.alt: A Hewlett-Packard HP 9000 B-class B180L workstation with an HP A4032A 17-inch colour CRT, running HP-UX 10.20 with CDE
images.caption: A B180L with the smaller 17-inch HP CRT. The B-class carried PCI, 100 Mbit LAN, 16-bit audio and Visualize-EG graphics on the board — the machine QEMU's B160L model reproduces.

images.alt: A Hewlett-Packard HP 9000 B180L workstation, PA-RISC 7300LC at 180 MHz
images.caption: The B180L system unit — a low, wide desktop box around a 180 MHz PA-7300LC, the processor family this station's emulated B160L runs.

images.alt: The system board of a Hewlett-Packard HP 9000 B180L workstation, PA-RISC 7300LC CPU, with memory, SCSI and Visualize graphics on board
images.caption: Inside: the B180L system board with the PA-7300LC, its memory and the on-board SCSI and Visualize graphics — the LASI/Dino chipset that HP-UX 10.20's install kernel had to be recent enough to drive.
